stratcomments: Lower-middle Racine Formation, probably mid-Wenlockian.
lithdescript: Very fossiliferous. This is a typical Wenlockian carbonate mud mound community, in which the core contains mostly carbonate mud, sometimes with Stromatactis-like structures, and echinoderm debris and the flank beds are echinoderm-dominated. Skeletal grains in the flank beds which contain this community can be either moldic or dolomite-replaced, and the texture ranges from non-cherty, porous dolowackestone to dolopackstone, with some grainstone present also in the flank facies, to crystalline dolomudstones and sparse dolowaxkestone to dolopackstone, with some grainstone present also in the flank facies, to crystalline dolomudstones and sparse dolowackestones in the cores. Skeletal grains show the full range from well to poorly sorted, and some graded bedding is present in the inclined beds of the echinoderm facies. Corals, which tend to surround the mound core, are sometimes overturned (Philcox, 1970), and in any case, are not abundant enough to form an organic framework. As noted by Witzke (1981b, 1987b), the general absence of skeletal boundstone fabrics precludes interpretation as an organic-framework reef, but the presence of apparent penecontemporaneous cave and fissure-fills in the core, often with thick trilobite or nautiloid concentrations, plus wedge-shaped debris flows in some facies, suggests that the mounds were rigid features, possibly resulting from submarine cementation processes (Witzke, 1987a). Dolomitized botryoidal and fibrous marine cembents are present. Sedimentary features are consistent with episodic high-energy conditions, such as would result from storm action in depths generally at or slightly below fair weather wave base.

(1996). Geol. Rundsch 85:278-292; "...this unit consists of a carbonate platform with reef mounds and surrounding shoal sediments of mostly pure biodetritic and pleoidal limestones. Here slow and discontinuous accumulation of carbonate material continued in a very shallow water but under normal marine conditions....to the south and southwest the carbonate platform passes with a conspicuous slope into a deeper shelf basin where a uniform alternation of micritic limestones and marls accumulated." lithdescript: Ref. 11073: "Eke Beds (15m): Near the east coast of Gotland the boundary between Hemse and Eke Beds is marked by a hard-ground-like discontinuity plane overlain by detritic limestones and small reefmounds with stromatolitic algal deposits. collection_name: Hamra Beds: Fossils of Hoburgen-type reef limestone (Manten 1971, Table IX)
lithdescript: Ref. 11073: "Hamra/Sundre Beds (50m): The oolitic limestones of the upper Burgsvik Beds pass into oncolites with bioclasts of normal marine fauna. At Hoburgen, in the SW part of Gotland, these are overlain by a series of massive bioherms surrounded and covered by detritic and coarse crinoidal limestones (Sundre Beds). To the NE these platform deposits are replaced by micritic and argillaceous limestones with back reef character and often with an impoverished benthic fauna. Southwards, the carbonate platform of Hoburgen passes into a shelf basin area with the deposition of a limestone-marl sequence which then grades into off-reef shelf sediments ("Beyrichia Limestone") south of Gotland."

collection_comments: Arnold (1934, p.75): It is generally assumed that the Antrim shale and other shales of similar age were deposited in a body of water of considerable extent, and the contained vegetable fossils represent material which had been transported for some considerable distance and subjected to prolonged weathering. geogcomments: "Type locality (this list): black gastropod limestones ('Hercynella beds' -- 'Seewarte Kalke'), Monte Coglians = Seewarte west slope section, near Sentiero Spinotti, Carnic Alps, Italy. lithdescript: "The community usually occurs in bituminous pelmicrites with bioclasts, rarely interbedded with oolitic limestones. The organic matter content is high to very high."
geology_comments: "A subtidal restricted (high salinity and temperature) and protected (low energy and oxygen) lagoonal environment is assumed, in which ephemeral storm waves could transport bioclasts or even biosomata from the back reef or even the reef front. This community is intimately associated with the Amphipora Community and prepresents a limited part of its environment, with persisten subtidal conditions and still, partly active water exchange with the open sea. An outer BA 3 depth is suggested...it is thought to represent relatively discontinous depressions almost completely surround by BA 2, in close connection with reef complex."
collection_comments: Despite geographic range of communities similar to this, presentation suggests all elements listed are present together in type locality.
taxonomy_comments: Only dominant members of each group seem to be listed.

geology_comments: "A regularly repeated, shallowing upwards, subtidal to supratidal cyclothem (consisting of the following triplet from bottom: (a) gastropod-oncoid rich algal-pellet calcarenite, subtidal; (b) laminated algal stromatolite, intertidal; ;(c) massive birds eye rich micrite, supratidal, is developed here. A high energy, very shallow subtidal to intertidal environment is assumed for this community in a restricted by euphotic-phytal zone...A BA 1 to 2 position is suggested."

These beds rest unconformably on a layer of sandy mudstones of Middle Silurian age. The fossiliferous beds, about nine meters above the base of the Upper Devonian stratum, are composed mainly of mudstones.
geology_comments: Rhizomes and branches are in organic connection, indicating that the sediments were autochthonously deposited in quiet water.

collection_name: Proetus concinnus-Warburgella stokesii Assemblage, Much Wenlock Limestone
geogcomments: Dudley, West Midlands, Nat'l Grid Ref. SO 9355 9185. Town of Dudley is reference for coordinates.
lithdescript: "..several lithofacies...Trilobites most common in interbedded lst and silty mudst. and nodular lst. lithofacies. The lst. beds and nodules variously consist of carbonate mudstone, grainstone, packstone, and wackestone. "
geology_comments: "Level-bottom carbonate shelf...This is a BA 3 unit....several lithofacies...Trilobites most common in interbedded lst and silty mudst. and nodular lst. lithofacies. The lst. beds and nodules variously consist of carbonate mudstone, grainstone, packstone, and wackestone. Microfacies analysis indicates that the nodular lst. was depos. below storm wave base, although algae indicate photic zone..Deposition of interbedded lst and silty mudst in somewhat shallower water, up to depths approaching normal wave base. In view of wide extent of local Wenlock shelf and consequent attenuation of wave activity, the actual depths would not have been great. A well-oxygenated, mid-shelf location for the assemblage was envisaged by Ratcliffe (1988)."
collection_comments: The Assemblage type is broadly distributed, but it seems fairly clear from the text that the elements listed here are known from the Much Wenlock Limestone.

The jasper cherts are predominantly cherry-red, but range to orange and gray. ... The jasper contains nodules, pockets, and irregular lenticular pods of white quartz and chalcedony, generally 5 to 15 cm in length.
geology_comments: Mcbride and Thomson (1970) interpret the paleoenvironment to be deep-water, whereas Folk (1970) interprets the early environment to be shallow-water, peritidal.
collection_methods: selective quarrying,peel or thin section,field collection

collection_name: Helokybe-Encrinurus-Richterarges Assemblage of the Read Bay Fm., Cornwallis Is.
geogcomments: "Goodsir Creek, Cornwallis Island, where it occurs at two groups of horizons, respectively 120-170 m (Geol.Surv.Can. localities 95229-32) and 335-345 m (GSC loc's 95234-35) above the base of the section. The former group of horizons is designated as the type."
lithdescript: "Most of the trilobites were found in highly fossiliferous calcareous mudstones and wackestones, in which traction current structures are very rare."
geology_comments: "Level-bottom carbonate shelf...BA 2, shallow marine subtidal. The fossils are generally undamaged and articulated. Thin beds of shelly and intraclastic packstone (with scoured based) ...present at irregular intervals. [Strata probably] deposited between wave base and storm wave base."\r\nSEP environmental call based on given info.

collection_comments: Counts are given for trilobites. It seems implicit that all elements are known from type locality, even though the community is more widely distributed.

geology_comments: "[Set of two related communities]: Developed in marginal part of extensive shallows with mobile sediments containing structures indicating a lot of physical transport, belonging to different facies and dense benthic populations forming biostromes and coquinas. [This community]: The burial sites for the Megalomus (articulated and disarticulated; ratios of L and R valves commonly about equal) are near their life sites. Shallow water unit, in about the BA 2-3 position, within the zone of intense photosynthesis for blue-green algae, and skeletal grains forming on local shallows in the rough water region."

geogcomments: Tareya River section, on the lower Tareya River, a tributary of the Pyasino River in central Taimyr, some 45 km from its mouth. Community said to have geographic range of central Taimyr, but it seems clear that material listed is present at type locality, from which communities are said to be selected.
lithdescript: See geology. "The fossils occur in the light-greenish gray mudstone"
geology_comments: "The 500 m thick section is built up predominantly of argillaceous carbonate deposits. The base contains gypsum, argillaceous dolomites, siltstones (Belyi Kamen subhorizon, Ust' Taryeya horizon, the equivalent of the Lower Lochkovian) grading up section into rhythmically interbedded carbonate and argillaceous rocks (the Uryun and Tolbat subhorizons of the Ust' Tareya horizon; Daksan, Yunkhoda, Taribigai subhorizons, the Zlobin horizon; the Trigonirhynchia postventricos and Favosites regularissimus zones, equivalents of the Lochkovian-Zlichovian), there are also variegated siltstones, marls, dolomites (the Wijdeaspis arctica zone, the end of the Lower Devonian. The section shows a cyclic development...(carbonate beds with basal argillaceous units) while the general trend was regressive-transgressive-regressive...absence of channel facies...There are a number of communities showing a trend in the development of environments from gypsiferous lagoons to open marine basins, beginning basally with A and extending upwards into F, namely: A. Fish-Phyllopod; B. Lingula-Phyllopod; C. Pelecypod-Phyllopod; D. Eurypterid-Pelecypod; E. Howellella-Tiverina; F. Rhombopora-Hebetoechia...hypersaline at bottom to normal marine at top." "BA 1 is shown by rhynchonellids, with a position close to BA 2 shown by Howellella. The salinity was probably nearl normal as shown by the greater abundance of bivalves and rare articulate brachiopods."

lithdescript: "Abundantly fossiliferous. The lithology is a very porous, noncherty skeletal-moldic, dolopackstone to grainstone."
geology_comments: "whole cyclocrinitid thalli sometimes well size-sorted and tightly packed into distinct layers or thin units, but more random dense aggregations also observed, and sekeltal grains and whole fossils not well sorted. At type loc. interfingers locally with Stricklandia lens ultima Assoc. and Bolicrinus-Theleproktocrinus Assoc. below and with overlying Harpidium (isovella) maquoketa Assoc...Echinoderm debris common..occasional whole cups noted...This is most probably storm generated, as it is unlikely that fragile thecae or thalli would stand up to much transport or to regular disturbance...outer BA 3 to shallow BA 4 seems likely."
collection_comments: Echinoderm and Cyclocrinites (algae) abundances given in table 45.22.

geogcomments: Type loc.: Monticello quarry, loc. 33 of Witzke and Strimple ('81), 'flank beds', Jones Co., Iowa. Distributed elsewhere in Silurian outcrop belt of E. Iowa

lithdescript: "This comm. occurs in the so-called flank beds around a central carbonate mound core consisting of dense dolomudstones with a limited megafauna of large colonial rugose and tabulate corals and scattered crinoidal debris. The bulk of the echinoderms occur in flanking crinoidal packstones and grainstones, some displaying graded bedding. These represent debris flows around the carbonate mounds."
geology_comments: "Echinoderms found both as intact cups and as large debris pieces...occasional root systems..this does not appear to be a thicket community...mound core BA 3...flank facies shallow-middle BA 4"
collection_comments: Echinoderm abundances given in table 45.26. This collection overlaps somewhat with PBDB coll. 24963.

collection_name: Bolicrinus-Theleproktocrinus Assoc., Farmers Creek Mbr., East-Central Iowa
geogcomments: Localities include Frost Quarrry, Jackson Co.; Behrends Quarry, Jones Co.; C. W. Martin Quarry, Dubuque County; Johns Creek Quarry, Dubuque Co. (Jones Co. is basis of coordinates.)

lithdescript: "The lithology is very porous, chert-free, finely crystalline dolomite. Witzke (1981a) describes a range of skeletal-moldic wackestone to packstone fabrics...with some dolomitic replacement of skeletal grains: all have been noted in rocks containing this association."
geology_comments: "..intact thecae and cups...varying amounts of disarticulated debris...holdfasts and root systems uncommon...evidence for deposition of the whole of the Farmers Creek Member generally below wave base, with only occasional storm disturbances...Witzke and Johnson [ref. 7006] interpret the F.C. as ranging between BA 3 and 4..The preponderance of evidence favors outer BA3-4..."\r\n\r\nSEP environmental call based on given description and same vol. page 807.
collection_comments: I have combined four separate collections listed, with abundances, in table 45.38, as well as other taxa mentioned in text. (Table includes echinoderms and brachiopods only.) Community is said to be similar to Stricklandia laevis Community of Witzke and Johnson (1999, PBDB ref. 7006, PBDB coll. 25038), but the collections listed here are different from those listed in Witzke and Johnson.

collection_name: Callocystites-Lysocystites Assoc., Lower Welton Member, Eastern Iowa
geogcomments: Type loc.: Behr Quarry, lower 5 m, Welton Member, loc. 89 of Johnson ('77a), loc. 7 of Witzke and Strimple ('81), Clinton Co., Iowa. Distribution: Eastern Iowa Silurian outcrop belt.
stratcomments: "Late Llandovery (C5-C6) to Early Wenlockian...lower Welton Member"
lithdescript: "characterized by horizontally bedded, porous, abundantly fossiliferous (typically very crinoidal) non-cherty dolomite. Most skeletal debris preserved as molds, but beds containing dolomite-replaced skeletal debris are also noted (crinoidal wackestone and packstone fabrics)."
geology_comments: "thecae often intact...root systems and occasional complete crowns...unlikely that true thickes were present...carbonate mud mounds not present, but occur elsewhere in Scotch Grove...little evidence of skeletal grain abrasion, cross bedding, current sorting...The abundance of articulated echinoderm remains, among other evidence, suggests quiet depositional environment, below maximum storm wave base. This is the most diverse and most offshore fossil community in the Iowa Silurian. A position somewhere in the shallow BA 4 to BA 4-5 boundary spectrum is likely..."\r\n\r\nSEP environmental call based on given description and same vol. page 807.
collection_comments: Includes material from type locality (table 45.30, which gives abundances for echinoderms and brachiopods), as well as other taxa mentioned in text. The association is said to be part of the 'Costistricklandia' castellana-Eospirifer Community of Witzke and Johnson (PBDB coll. 24963), but the collections are not duplicates.
taxonomy_comments: Some 30 genera of brachiopods are said to be present, but not all are listed. (See collection comments.)

collection_name: Periechocrinus necis-Coelocystis subglobosus Assoc., Racine Fm.
geogcomments: Community known from NE Illinos and SE Wisconsin, Racine Formation and equivalents. Collection in table 43.31 is from Bridgeport Quarry, SE1/4 sec. 29, t39n, r14e, Englewood 7.5' quad, Chicago, Illinois, made by H.H. Hindshaw around 1875-85.
stratcomments: "Middle-Upper Wenlockian to Ludlovian...Racine Formation and equivalents. The community may occur only in the lower and middle Racine. Its presence has been confirmed at three of the classic Racine collecting sites, the Horlick Reef Complex (type locality for the Racine), the Bridgeport Reef, and the Hawthorne Reef..."
lithdescript: "Very fossiliferous. The most common lithology...is flat to inclined-bedded, porous, noncherty, finely crystalline crinoid-moldic dolopackstone, but dolograinstone and dolowackestone textures are also seen. At some sites (e.g., Bridgeport), the rock is overwhelmingly (better than 90%) echinoderm calices and debris..."
geology_comments: "...root systems and holdfasts scattered throughout, but major concentrations in thin intervals are also seen, i.e., crinoid thickets are developed....debris piles soemtimes winnowed and show small-=scale crossbeds...This is predominantly a mound associated but somewhat offshore, probably outer BA3 community..."\r\nSEP environmental call based on given information and regional context
collection_comments: I have included echinoderms and brachiopods listed (with abundances) in table 45.31, as well as other taxa mentioned in text.
taxonomy_comments: "It is entirely possible that the high species diversity is in part an artifact, as the fauna has not been revised since Weller (1900), and internal molds can be difficult to work with. On the other hand, detailed work with such material (e.g., Witzke 1976; Witzke and Strimbple 1981) has tended to increase total echinoderm diversity in lithologically similar units."

The predominance of small echinoderms and the high brachiopod diversity suggesta outer BA 4"\r\nSEP environmental call based on given info

collection_name: Pisocrinus (P.)-Ischadites tenuis Assoc., Sub-Brassfield, Indiana and Kentucky
geogcomments: Jefferson County, Indiana and Jefferson County, Kentucky. Type locality: silurian exposure along the N side of small drainage into Ohio R. near top of bluffs above Harts Fall Creek, NW1/4 NW1/4 sec. 30, T3N R10E, Madison West 7.5' Quadrangle, Jeff. Co., Ind.
stratcomments: "?Basal Silurian in southern Indiana and adjacent Kentucky (below the Brassfield Formation) and lying unconformably on the late Ordovician Saluda Dolomite--Wenlockian;possibly lower Llandoverian [This second occurrence seems to refer to distinct stratigraphic position, not type locality]...unnamed sub-Brassfield Silurian unit..."
lithdescript: "Moderately fossiliferous. The basic lithology is a porous, silty dolowackestone, with silicified fossil debris constituting no more than 40% of the rocks, most commonly less than 10%. The Laurel occurrences have some clastic silt, but the sub-Brassfield nearly lacks clastics, the abundant silt-sized particles being mostly small dolomite rhombs. Larger detrital grains include common glauconite and limonite..."
geology_comments: Material described as disaggregated, sometimes winnowed; voids as well as silica replacement. Interpreted as echinoderm shoal environment. (Shallow BA 4 for the related Laurel occurrences.)\r\nSEP environmental call based on given information and regional context

geogcomments: Type loc.: The Glen (formerly termed Willowvale), an eastern tributary of Sauquoit Creek, 2.5 km W of Bridgewater Street, New Hartford, Oneida County, NY (Utica West 7.5' Quad. Distribution: Central New York State.

geology_comments: "The occurrence of storm-winnowed coquinites with gutter casts and of rare hummocky laminated siltstones indicates deposition within storm wave base, but in a generally quiet environment. Most fossils disarticulated...Brachiopods mostly convex up, suggesting low sedimentation rates and minor current action...Bathymetric indicators include receptaculitids...as well as storm beds. [Brachiopods suggest BA 4.]"\r\n2003:04:06 SEP Environmental/tectonic/sequence call based on description and Brett et al. (1998). Bulletin New York State Museum 491:89-143. "Williamson-Willowvale interval has been interpretted as the early (maximum) highstand of Sequence IV" (p.107). Also by Lin and Brett (1988). Graptolites moderately common, finely disseminated carbonaceous matter present in small amounts...likely mid to outer Ba 4, only infrequently disturbed by storms. The low diversity is likely due to the very soft and relatively rapidly accumulating substrate..."\r\n2003.04.06: Environmenal call by S. Peters based on field experience with unit

stratcomments: "Early Silurian (early Llandovery), based on graptolites, i.e. zones 16-19 of the British succession (Berry and Boucot 1970)." [I.e., acuminatus through gregarius Zones, which would imply an age range of Rhuddanian through early Aeronian.]
lithdescript: "Witzke states that 'the Mosalem is the most argilalceous unit noted in the Silurian of Iowa and is primarily characterized by dense, thin-bedded argillaceous dolomites.' the unit is most shaly basally and more dolomitic at the top. Color varies from gray to brown. Locally there are chert nodules in the middle or upper portions. Major parts show a mottled coloration when weathered due to burrowing. Other parts are distinctly laminated, with laminations often less than 1 mm..."
geology_comments: Plants and other carbonaceous material noted, as well as soft-bodied "worms". Contact with underlying Maquoketa unconformable, with deeply eroded Maquoketa surface. "A nearshoe environment, equivalent to BA 1, seems indicated, although the presence of Leptaena would indicate at least BA 2 to 3 for at least one bedding plane...possible halite pseudomorphs and rare ripple marks low in the Iowa Mosalem section.." This is seen as the shallower-water variant of the Lecthyalus Community Group. Compare with PBDB coll. 25861.

collection_name: Xiangshuyuan Fm., Baisha Facies, Reef Lst., NE Border of C Guizhou Uplift
geogcomments: Formation occurs in Outcrop areas 73-78,81, and 82 of ref. 7624 (border region of Sichuan, Guizhou, Hubei, and Hunan Provinces). Counties in which this Baisha Facies is said to occur include Baisha, Shiqian, Sinan, Fenggan, and Zhengan. Shiqian County used as basis of coordinates.
stratcomments: Except where otherwise stated, ref. 7624 uses Lower Silurian as equivalent to Llandovery, Middle Silurian as equivalent to Wenlock, and Upper Silurian as equivalent to Ludlow plus Pridoli. "In light of the presence of Pristiograptus gregarius in the underlying formation, and the presence in the lower part of this formation of Borealis, it was assigned to the late Middle Llandoverian. The upper part of the formation containing Stricklandia, Merciella, Paraconchidium, and Virgianella was assigned to the earliest Late Llandovery." Above Lungmachi Fm. and below Leijiatun Fm.
lithdescript: "There are two sediment types included in the X. Fm., Baisha and Yinjiang. The Baisha type...is characterized by marl intercalated with shelly limestone and reef limestone. The shelly limestone includes abundant Paraconchidium and Virgianella, indicating low diversity, and the reef limestone includes...corals...stromatoporoids, and algae. The Yinjiang type is distributed to the NE of the Baisha type...and is characterized by mudstone, argillaceous limestone, and marl. Fossils are different from those of the Baisha type...[details]."
geology_comments: Correlation chart indicates BA3 based on shelly fauna at most localities, in some places BA3-4, and in some places graptolite-based ba3.

lithdescript:
Beds in type sections divided into a number of facies and subfacies:
A: "consists mainly of biogenic-clastic limestone." 
 A1: "coral limestones interbedded with siltstones and mudstones containing plant remains"
 A2: "massive reefal limestones" / "biogenic-clastic limestones, locally with coral bioherms"
B: "composed chiefly of mudstones"
 B1: "interbedded with limestones and richly fossiliferous"

collection_name: S2/f528 - Anthill Black Shale, Anthill Creek
geogcomments: SPECIFIC LOCATION: Twenty-two metres below waterfall, in Anthill Creek, 10 m downstream from S2/f565, Nelson, New Zealand. LAT/LONG: estimated based on Collingwood, Nelson.
stratcomments: STRATIGRAPHIC RELATIONS: Derived from Anthill Black Shale Member of Aorangi Mine Fm, which overlies the Malone Mbr (lower and middle Lancefieldian) and is overlain by the Battery Mb (upper Castlemainian and lower Yapeenian). THICKNESS: 150 m in type section. AGE: Zone of I. v. lunatus (upper part), corresponding to the upper part of the member and is hence upper early Castlemannian. STRATIGRAPHIC POSITION: Presumably upper part of Anthill Black Shale Mbr.
lithdescript: SPECIFIC LITHOLOGY: Extremely hard, siliceous, pyritic black shale and chert. LITHIFICATION: Lithified, as text states lithology to be "extremely hard".
geology_comments: ENVIRONMENT: Quiet bottom water, lack of circulation, plankton-rich, extreme paucity of incoming clastic detritus, slow persistent supply of biogenic silica. Environment of deposition presumed to be that of a starved offshore basin within or adjacent to a region of normal clastic deposition. Water depth likely to have been with the range of the bathyal depth zone.
preservation_comments: GENERAL TAPHONOMY: Presence of organic carbon, relatively abundant iron-sulphide, absence of benthonic or tarce fossils, abundant trace fossils, slow rate of deposition.
collection_comments: COLLECTOR: S.K. Swarko (1959). REPOSITORY: New Zealand Geological Survey (now GNS Science), Lower Hutt, New Zealand

"I recently shared in two articles some details related to the discovery of Ordovician fossils in a region located several kilometers south of Cerro Asperoand one kilometer northeast of the San Isidro ranch...The site is located within the Empozada Ravine and its surroundings; that is, a ravine situated further west of the Agua de la Cruz ravine and further northeast of the oldSan Isidro ravine."
stratcomments: The text states the collection stratigraphy to be "Lasheriana Formation, Empozadense Horizon...'Lower Ordovician, Upper Level" which is now obsolete and corresponds to the Empozada and Estancia San Isidro Formations (Abre et. al. in Lexico Estratigrafio de la Argentina vol III, 2025). Faunal lists likely correspond to Darriwilian age
lithdescript: Several lithologies listed but only one specifies fossils: "Right bank of the QUebrada de la Empozada. 1) Gray colizos, 2) Gray and greenish limestone strata with Cryptolithus, Encrinurus, Eoorthis, Leptaena, etc. 3) gray limestones and clays, 4) deposit with angular glocks (tilites); 5) gray limestones and clays, 6) thin beds of silicified limestones, 7) gray limestones and clays. All from the Lower Ordovician, Upper Level"

stratcomments: Conodonts from this section indicate that the reef-stromatoporoid bioherms can be correlated to the Belodina confluens conodont Biozone, indicating an early Katian (Ka-1) age
lithdescript: 141-m-thick sequence of dark-colored mudstone, thin-layered nodular limestone, and reef stromatoporoid bioherms at the top. The formation extends across northwestern Tarim, but the thick-bedded reef-stromatoporoid bioherms are only known in the eastern part of the Kalpintag Range.

geogcomments: Station 242NB (=552NB), cliff extending about 100 yards (91.44 m) along the northwestern shore of Snake Island, about 0.2 mile (0.32 km) from the north tip of the island, southwest side of Dawson Bay, Lake Winnipegosis. Beds deformed into a broad gentle anticlinal fold.
stratcomments: Text assigns unit to MIDDLE DEVONIAN, Dawson Bay Formation Member B, Unit 2. Dawson Bay Formation is regionally correlated with the Givetian stage of the Western Canada Sedimentary Basin; assigned to Elk Point Group based on standard Manitoba Devonian stratigraphic nomenclature (not stated explicitly in text).
lithdescript: Limestone, argillaceous, medium brown, fine grained, irregular bedding, beds up to 0.7 foot (0.21 m) thick, weathers pale orange-brown and medium brownish grey, contains dark grey to black bituminous material, finely disseminated iron sulphide also present, transitional upper contact, megafossils sparse.
geology_comments: Argillaceous limestone with dark grey to black bituminous (organic-rich) material and finely disseminated iron sulphide suggests low-energy, restricted-circulation conditions; sparse megafossils and transitional contact support a restricted shallow subtidal/lagoonal interpretation within the broader Dawson Bay carbonate-evaporite platform sequence.
collection_comments: Repository: GSC (fossils sent to GSC index collection).
